# Merge gate

The merge step belongs to the delivery lead. It checks facts, it does not re-review the code.

## Conditions, read fresh from the live pull request every time

- The pull request base is the default branch and its body links the driving task (or it is a bet's final review pull request).
- The reviewer has posted a formal review that passes it in substance, keyed to the current head commit. A review keyed to an older head does not count.
- The risk the reviewer named is low or medium. A high risk pull request waits for a person who owns the repository, named on the task.
- CI on the current head is green. If CI is still running, turn on auto-merge so the code host merges the moment it is green, and move on. Never end a session watching CI.
- No do-not-merge or hold note on the task or the pull request.
- The branch has no real conflict with the default branch.

## Rules

- Never update a pull request branch from the default branch to get it merged. Each update pushes a new head, restarts CI and voids the review, so the queue never drains. A pull request that is only behind merges as it is.
- Do not create a timer or one-off trigger per pull request. The merge sweep covers merges, and auto-merge covers a pull request waiting on CI. If a merge truly cannot wait, use a status-change trigger on the task.
- Needing a merge tool you do not have is a missing credential: say so on the task and ask the agent that holds the connection. Do not work around it with other tools.
- A red check on the default branch is the delivery lead's to close the same day: find the pull request that turned it red from the failing log lines, get a fix task started for the developer, and follow it through the reviewer and the merge step.

## When a condition fails

Send it back: one task comment that @mentions the reviewer and names the pull request, the head commit and the failed condition, then move the task from validated to in_review. A comment alone is not a send-back. Never send the same head back twice.

## After a merge

Move the task from validated to done. If the pull request belongs to a bet, check the bet: when every build task is done, every pull request of the bet is merged and the deploy is confirmed (or none is needed), the bet can go from active to live. Waiting for first events, a long measurement task or the won or lost call never blocks that move; put them on follow-up tasks or the bet's check date. Moving a bet from define to active, or from live to succeeded or failed, needs a person's go.

# Task handoff discipline

The Product Delivery flow is event-driven. Triggers fire on a status change and nothing else. A task already sitting in the right status emits no event when you comment on it, so the next agent is never started and the task strands silently.

**The rule: every action that hands work to another agent must either move the task's status or @mention that agent in the comment. Never neither.**

## The statuses

backlog, todo, in_progress, in_review, validated, done. Moving to todo starts the developer. in_progress is the developer's to work. in_review starts the reviewer. validated means passed review and queued for the merge step. It does not mean blocked.

## Creating a task

A task created straight at todo emits a created event, not a status change, so the developer's trigger stays silent. Create the task at backlog and then update it to todo, or create it at todo and @mention the driver in a comment in the same turn.

## Handing a task back

- A pull request that is behind the default branch, red CI, or a rebase or push needed: set the task to todo and @mention the developer. A manual send-back from in_review to in_progress also starts the developer.
- A verdict that is missing or stale and needs a fresh one: move the task from validated to in_review. That starts the reviewer again.
- A block only a person can clear (a credential, an account, a repository setting): leave the status, comment on the task naming the exact action and the person who can do it.
- Re-passing a task that is already validated: the status is already right, so @mention the delivery lead so the merge step is started.

A hold that leaves a task at validated with no comment or move is a failure. A comment on its own is not a hand-back. After you move a task back, check with list_sessions that an agent is really running on it, and if not, start one.
